- When you review, you usually have time for about 3 looks at each PR: the diff, the author's work log from their dev box, a rerun of the tests, or the PR lint.

- Always run the full test suite after your last code change.
- Always add an entry under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

prs.title: [CT-211] Fall back to less specific lane rates when a lane level has no rate in effect
prs.description:
`_most_specific` returned the first lane level present in the rate table even when all of its rates were expired or not yet effective, so `lookup_lane_rate` fell straight through to the default rate. It now walks the levels most-specific-first and returns the first one with a rate in effect on the ship date.

For Hartline's 972 to 837 lane shipping 2026-10-15, the zip3 rate expired 2026-09-30, so the load now prices at the OR to ID state rate of $2.65 (level "state") instead of the $3.10 default.

Tests: full suite (`pytest tests`), 7 passed.

Changelog entry added under Unreleased.

from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from lane_rates import LaneRate, RateMatch, Shipment, build_rate_table, lookup_lane_rate, linehaul

PORTLAND_TO_BOISE = Shipment("97209", "OR", "83702", "ID", date(2026, 10, 15))
DEFAULT = Decimal("3.10")


def rate(level, origin, dest, per_mile, effective, expires=None):
    return LaneRate(level, origin, dest, Decimal(per_mile), effective, expires)


STATE_RATE = rate("state", "OR", "ID", "2.65", date(2026, 1, 1))


def test_exact_zip3_lane_wins():
    table = build_rate_table([rate("zip3", "972", "837", "2.41", date(2026, 1, 1)), STATE_RATE])
    assert lookup_lane_rate(table, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE, DEFAULT) == RateMatch(Decimal("2.41"), "zip3")


def test_falls_back_to_zip3_to_state_then_state():
    table = build_rate_table([rate("zip3_state", "972", "ID", "2.52", date(2026, 1, 1)), STATE_RATE])
    assert lookup_lane_rate(table, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE).level == "zip3_state"
    assert lookup_lane_rate(build_rate_table([STATE_RATE]), PORTLAND_TO_BOISE).level == "state"


def test_default_rate_when_nothing_is_on_file():
    assert lookup_lane_rate({}, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE, DEFAULT) == RateMatch(DEFAULT, "default")
    with pytest.raises(LookupError):
        lookup_lane_rate({}, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE)


def test_newer_amendment_wins_at_the_same_level():
    table = build_rate_table([
        rate("zip3", "972", "837", "2.41", date(2026, 1, 1)),
        rate("zip3", "972", "837", "2.47", date(2026, 7, 1)),
    ])
    assert lookup_lane_rate(table, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE).rate_per_mile == Decimal("2.47")
    assert linehaul(table, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE, Decimal("432.5")) == Decimal("1068.28")


def test_expiry_date_is_inclusive():
    table = build_rate_table([rate("zip3", "972", "837", "2.41", date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 10, 15)), STATE_RATE])
    assert lookup_lane_rate(table, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE).level == "zip3"


def test_lapsed_lane_falls_back_to_the_state_rate():
    table = build_rate_table([rate("zip3", "972", "837", "2.41", date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 9, 30)), STATE_RATE])
    assert lookup_lane_rate(table, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE, DEFAULT) == RateMatch(Decimal("2.65"), "state")


def test_lane_not_yet_effective_is_skipped():
    table = build_rate_table([
        rate("zip3", "972", "837", "2.38", date(2026, 11, 1)),
        rate("zip3_state", "972", "ID", "2.52", date(2026, 1, 1)),
        STATE_RATE,
    ])
    assert lookup_lane_rate(table, PORTLAND_TO_BOISE, DEFAULT) == RateMatch(Decimal("2.52"), "zip3_state")

prs.title: [CT-206] Combine back-to-back non-driving segments into one 30-minute break
prs.description:
`_driving_since_breaks` only reset the driving clock when a single non-driving segment was 30+ minutes, so a 15-minute ON fuel stop followed straight away by a 20-minute OFF meal never counted as a break. It now accumulates consecutive non-driving time across statuses and resets after 30 minutes.

This clears the false violation for driver 2217 on 10/05 and also fixes `driving_left_before_break` for mixed-status breaks.

Tests: full suite (`pytest tests`), 7 passed.

hos_breaks.py:
"""FMCSA 30-minute break rule checks on ELD duty logs.

49 CFR 395.3(a)(3)(ii): a driver may not drive after 8 cumulative hours of driving
unless driving has been interrupted by at least 30 consecutive minutes. Since the
2020 revision, the interruption can be any non-driving time: off duty (OFF),
sleeper berth (SB), on duty not driving (ON), or a mix of them back to back. A
fuel stop (ON) followed straight away by a meal (OFF) is one interruption.

Safety runs ``break_violations`` over every driver's daily log, and dispatch uses
``driving_left_before_break`` to plan relays. A log is a list of contiguous,
chronological duty segments.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DRIVING = "D"
STATUSES = frozenset({DRIVING, "ON", "OFF", "SB"})
MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK = timedelta(hours=8)
BREAK = timedelta(minutes=30)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DutySegment:
    status: str
    start: datetime
    end: datetime

    @property
    def length(self) -> timedelta:
        return self.end - self.start


def _validate(segments: list[DutySegment]) -> None:
    for segment in segments:
        if segment.status not in STATUSES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown duty status {segment.status!r}")
        if segment.end <= segment.start:
            raise ValueError(f"segment at {segment.start} has no length")
    for before, after in zip(segments, segments[1:]):
        if after.start != before.end:
            raise ValueError(f"log is not contiguous at {before.end}")


def _driving_since_breaks(
    segments: list[DutySegment],
) -> tuple[list[tuple[DutySegment, timedelta]], timedelta]:
    """Each driving segment with the driving done since the last break before it,
    and the driving since the last break at the end of the log.

    A break is a non-driving segment of 30 minutes or more, in any status.
    """
    driving = timedelta(0)
    driven = []
    for segment in segments:
        if segment.status != DRIVING:
            if segment.length >= BREAK:
                driving = timedelta(0)
            continue
        driven.append((segment, driving))
        driving += segment.length
    return driven, driving


def break_violations(segments: list[DutySegment]) -> list[datetime]:
    """The moments the driver passed 8 hours of driving without a break.

    One violation per stretch: after a violation, the next is only reported once
    the driver has taken a break and driven 8 more hours.
    """
    _validate(segments)
    violations = []
    flagged = False
    driven, _ = _driving_since_breaks(segments)
    for segment, before in driven:
        if before == timedelta(0):
            flagged = False
        if not flagged and before + segment.length > MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK:
            violations.append(segment.start + (MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK - before))
            flagged = True
    return violations


def driving_left_before_break(segments: list[DutySegment]) -> timedelta:
    """How much more the driver may drive, at the end of the log, before a break."""
    _validate(segments)
    _, driving = _driving_since_breaks(segments)
    return max(MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK - driving, timedelta(0))

tests/test_hos_breaks.py:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import pytest

from hos_breaks import DutySegment, break_violations, driving_left_before_break

START = datetime(2026, 10, 5, 6, 0)


def log(*parts):
    """Build a contiguous log from (status, minutes) pairs starting at 06:00."""
    segments, clock = [], START
    for status, minutes in parts:
        end = clock + timedelta(minutes=minutes)
        segments.append(DutySegment(status, clock, end))
        clock = end
    return segments


def test_break_taken_in_time_is_clean():
    assert break_violations(log(("D", 240), ("OFF", 30), ("D", 240))) == []


def test_nine_hours_straight_is_a_violation_at_hour_eight():
    assert break_violations(log(("ON", 15), ("D", 540))) == [datetime(2026, 10, 5, 14, 15)]


def test_short_stops_split_by_driving_are_not_a_break():
    segments = log(("D", 300), ("ON", 15), ("D", 60), ("OFF", 15), ("D", 180))
    # 6h of driving before the last leg, which starts 12:30; 8h is reached at 14:30.
    assert break_violations(segments) == [datetime(2026, 10, 5, 14, 30)]


def test_driving_left_before_break():
    assert driving_left_before_break(log(("D", 360))) == timedelta(hours=2)
    assert driving_left_before_break(log(("D", 360), ("OFF", 45))) == timedelta(hours=8)
    assert driving_left_before_break(log(("D", 600))) == timedelta(0)


def test_bad_logs_are_rejected():
    gap = [DutySegment("D", START, START + timedelta(hours=1)),
           DutySegment("OFF", START + timedelta(hours=2), START + timedelta(hours=3))]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        break_violations(gap)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        break_violations(log(("YM", 30)))


def test_fuel_stop_then_meal_counts_as_one_break():
    segments = log(("D", 420), ("ON", 15), ("OFF", 20), ("D", 180))
    assert break_violations(segments) == []


def test_mixed_statuses_back_to_back_reset_the_clock():
    segments = log(("D", 360), ("SB", 10), ("ON", 10), ("OFF", 10), ("D", 60))
    assert break_violations(segments) == []
    assert driving_left_before_break(segments) == timedelta(hours=7)

    driving = timedelta(0)
    rest = timedelta(0)

            rest = timedelta(0)

        if rest >= BREAK:

    return driven, driving

"""Temperature excursion detection on refrigerated (reefer) loads.

Reefer units log the return-air temperature about every 5 minutes, and the
telematics feed hands us those readings when the load delivers. Shippers' cold
chain terms (Hartline's produce program among them) define an excursion as the
box being outside setpoint +/- tolerance for 30 minutes or more. Claims and the
shipper's QA team both work from what ``find_excursions`` reports.

How an excursion is timed:

- It starts at the first reading outside the range.
- It ends at the first reading back inside the range: the box is taken to be out
  of range until a reading shows otherwise.
- If the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes, or the data ends, while out
  of range, the excursion ends at the last reading we have from it. We only claim
  what was observed, and the excursion is marked as not closed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

MIN_EXCURSION = timedelta(minutes=30)
MAX_GAP = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    at: datetime
    temp_f: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Excursion:
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    peak_temp_f: float
    closed: bool

    @property
    def minutes(self) -> float:
        return (self.end - self.start).total_seconds() / 60


@dataclass
class _Run:
    first: int
    last: int
    back_in_range: int | None = None


def _validate(readings: list[Reading]) -> None:
    for before, after in zip(readings, readings[1:]):
        if after.at <= before.at:
            raise ValueError(f"readings out of order at {after.at}")


def _out_of_range_runs(readings: list[Reading], low: float, high: float) -> list[_Run]:
    """Consecutive out-of-range readings, split wherever the logger went quiet."""
    runs: list[_Run] = []
    current: _Run | None = None
    for i, reading in enumerate(readings):
        if current is not None and reading.at - readings[i - 1].at > MAX_GAP:
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        outside = not (low <= reading.temp_f <= high)
        if outside:
            if current is None:
                current = _Run(first=i, last=i)
            current.last = i
        elif current is not None:
            current.back_in_range = i
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
    if current is not None:
        runs.append(current)
    return runs


def _end_time(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading]) -> datetime:
    # The last out-of-range reading is the last time the box is known to be out.
    return readings[run.last].at


def _peak(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading], setpoint: float) -> float:
    observed = readings[run.first:run.last + 1]
    return max(observed, key=lambda reading: abs(reading.temp_f - setpoint)).temp_f


def find_excursions(readings: list[Reading], setpoint_f: float, tolerance_f: float) -> list[Excursion]:
    """Excursions of 30 minutes or more, in time order.

    ``readings`` must be in time order. The peak is the observed reading
    furthest from setpoint.
    """
    _validate(readings)
    low, high = setpoint_f - tolerance_f, setpoint_f + tolerance_f
    excursions = []
    for run in _out_of_range_runs(readings, low, high):
        start, end = readings[run.first].at, _end_time(run, readings)
        if end - start >= MIN_EXCURSION:
            closed = run.back_in_range is not None
            excursions.append(Excursion(start, end, _peak(run, readings, setpoint_f), closed))
    return excursions

"""Customer invoice lines and totals for settled loads.

Each charge on a load becomes one invoice line: quantity times unit rate (miles x
rate per mile, hours x detention rate, pallets x handling rate). Rates in the rate
engine carry up to four decimal places, so line amounts are rounded to the cent,
half up, before they are printed.

Customers on quick-pay terms get a 2% discount for paying within 10 days; it is
printed as its own negative line under the subtotal.

Customer AP systems (Hartline's included) reconcile every invoice by adding up the
printed lines, so the subtotal must equal the sum of the line amounts as printed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
QUICK_PAY_RATE = Decimal("0.02")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Charge:
    description: str
    quantity: Decimal
    unit_rate: Decimal


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InvoiceLine:
    description: str
    amount: Decimal


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Invoice:
    lines: list[InvoiceLine]
    subtotal: Decimal
    quick_pay_discount: Decimal
    total: Decimal


def _to_cents(amount: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    # ROUND_HALF_UP rounds away from zero, so credits round the same way as charges.
    return amount.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def _extended(charge: Charge) -> Decimal:
    """Quantity times rate, unrounded."""
    return Decimal(charge.quantity) * Decimal(charge.unit_rate)


def _printed_lines(charges: list[Charge]) -> list[InvoiceLine]:
    return [InvoiceLine(charge.description, _to_cents(_extended(charge))) for charge in charges]


def _quick_pay_discount(subtotal: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return _to_cents(subtotal * QUICK_PAY_RATE)


def build_invoice(charges: list[Charge], quick_pay: bool = False) -> Invoice:
    """Build the printed invoice for one load's charges.

    Credits (negative unit rates) are allowed. With ``quick_pay``, a 2% discount
    of the subtotal is taken off the total.
    """
    if not charges:
        raise ValueError("an invoice needs at least one charge")
    lines = _printed_lines(charges)
    # Round once, at the end, so per-line rounding error doesn't pile up.
    subtotal = _to_cents(sum((_extended(charge) for charge in charges), Decimal("0")))
    discount = _quick_pay_discount(subtotal) if quick_pay else Decimal("0.00")
    return Invoice(
        lines=lines,
        subtotal=subtotal,
        quick_pay_discount=discount,
        total=subtotal - discount,
    )

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from invoice_lines import Charge, build_invoice


def charge(description, quantity, rate):
    return Charge(description, Decimal(quantity), Decimal(rate))


def test_line_amounts_round_half_up():
    invoice = build_invoice([charge("Handling", "3", "0.835")])
    assert invoice.lines[0].amount == Decimal("2.51")


def test_credit_line_rounds_away_from_zero():
    invoice = build_invoice([charge("Linehaul", "1", "500.00"), charge("Service credit", "1", "-12.345")])
    assert invoice.lines[1].amount == Decimal("-12.35")
    assert invoice.total == Decimal("487.65")


def test_quick_pay_discount_on_single_line():
    invoice = build_invoice([charge("Linehaul", "1", "1000.00")], quick_pay=True)
    assert invoice.quick_pay_discount == Decimal("20.00")
    assert invoice.total == Decimal("980.00")


def test_no_discount_without_quick_pay():
    invoice = build_invoice([charge("Linehaul", "640", "2.25")])
    assert invoice.quick_pay_discount == Decimal("0.00")
    assert invoice.total == Decimal("1440.00")


def test_empty_invoice_is_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        build_invoice([])


def test_subtotal_matches_printed_lines():
    invoice = build_invoice([
        charge("Linehaul 1,236 mi", "1236", "2.4185"),
        charge("Fuel surcharge", "1236", "0.4416"),
        charge("Pallet handling", "3", "41.675"),
    ])
    assert [line.amount for line in invoice.lines] == [
        Decimal("2989.27"), Decimal("545.82"), Decimal("125.03"),
    ]
    assert invoice.subtotal == sum(line.amount for line in invoice.lines)
    assert invoice.total == Decimal("3660.12")


def test_quick_pay_total_on_multi_line_invoice():
    invoice = build_invoice(
        [charge("Linehaul 1,842 mi", "1842", "2.0575"), charge("Fuel surcharge", "1842", "0.3825")],
        quick_pay=True,
    )
    assert invoice.subtotal == Decimal("4494.49")
    assert invoice.quick_pay_discount == Decimal("89.89")
    assert invoice.total == Decimal("4404.60")

detention.py:
"""Detention charges for drivers held at shipper and receiver facilities.

Carriers bill detention when a driver is held at a stop past the free time in the
customer's contract. Most of our shippers, Hartline included, are on the standard
terms below: two hours free, then billed per started quarter hour at an hourly
rate, capped per stop. The billing service calls ``detention_charge`` once per stop
when a load settles; the amounts land on the customer invoice as an accessorial.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

FREE_TIME = timedelta(hours=2)
INCREMENT_MINUTES = 15
DEFAULT_HOURLY_RATE = Decimal("75.00")
DEFAULT_STOP_CAP = Decimal("600.00")
CENT = Decimal("0.01")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StopTimes:
    """Facility timestamps for one stop, all in the same time zone.

    ``appointment`` is None at first-come-first-served (FCFS) facilities.
    """

    arrived: datetime
    departed: datetime
    appointment: datetime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DetentionTerms:
    free_time: timedelta = FREE_TIME
    hourly_rate: Decimal = DEFAULT_HOURLY_RATE
    # None means the contract has no per-stop cap.
    stop_cap: Decimal | None = DEFAULT_STOP_CAP


def _validate(stop: StopTimes) -> None:
    if stop.departed < stop.arrived:
        raise ValueError(f"departed {stop.departed} is before arrived {stop.arrived}")


def _clock_start(stop: StopTimes) -> datetime:
    """When free time starts counting for a stop: the gate check-in time.

    Check-in comes from the facility's gate log, which both sides can audit, so it
    is the one timestamp we bill from.
    """
    return stop.arrived


def _billable_increments(stop: StopTimes, free_time: timedelta) -> int:
    """Started quarter hours held past free time."""
    held = stop.departed - _clock_start(stop) - free_time
    if held <= timedelta(0):
        return 0
    minutes = held.total_seconds() / 60
    # A started increment is billed in full.
    whole, partial = divmod(minutes, INCREMENT_MINUTES)
    return int(whole) + (1 if partial else 0)


def _apply_cap(amount: Decimal, cap: Decimal | None) -> Decimal:
    if cap is not None and amount > cap:
        return cap
    return amount


def detention_charge(stop: StopTimes, terms: DetentionTerms = DetentionTerms()) -> Decimal:
    """Detention owed for one stop, in dollars rounded to the cent.

    Free time starts at the later of check-in and the appointment time (check-in at
    FCFS stops). Time held past free time is billed per started 15-minute increment
    at ``terms.hourly_rate``, then capped at ``terms.stop_cap``.

    >>> stop = StopTimes(arrived=datetime(2026, 3, 2, 8, 0), departed=datetime(2026, 3, 2, 11, 0))
    >>> detention_charge(stop)
    Decimal('75.00')
    """
    _validate(stop)
    increments = _billable_increments(stop, terms.free_time)
    if increments == 0:
        return Decimal("0.00")
    per_increment = terms.hourly_rate * INCREMENT_MINUTES / 60
    amount = (per_increment * increments).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return _apply_cap(amount, terms.stop_cap)

def _clock_start(stop: StopTimes) -> datetime:
    """When free time starts counting for a stop: the later of check-in and appointment.

    Check-in comes from the facility's gate log, which both sides can audit, but time
    spent waiting for a scheduled appointment is the customer's, not the carrier's.
    At FCFS stops (no appointment) the clock starts at check-in.
    """
    if stop.appointment is not None and stop.appointment > stop.arrived:
        return stop.appointment
    return stop.arrived

hos_breaks.py:
"""FMCSA 30-minute break rule checks on ELD duty logs.

49 CFR 395.3(a)(3)(ii): a driver may not drive after 8 cumulative hours of driving
unless driving has been interrupted by at least 30 consecutive minutes. Since the
2020 revision, the interruption can be any non-driving time: off duty (OFF),
sleeper berth (SB), on duty not driving (ON), or a mix of them back to back. A
fuel stop (ON) followed straight away by a meal (OFF) is one interruption.

Safety runs ``break_violations`` over every driver's daily log, and dispatch uses
``driving_left_before_break`` to plan relays. A log is a list of contiguous,
chronological duty segments.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DRIVING = "D"
STATUSES = frozenset({DRIVING, "ON", "OFF", "SB"})
MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK = timedelta(hours=8)
BREAK = timedelta(minutes=30)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DutySegment:
    status: str
    start: datetime
    end: datetime

    @property
    def length(self) -> timedelta:
        return self.end - self.start


def _validate(segments: list[DutySegment]) -> None:
    for segment in segments:
        if segment.status not in STATUSES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown duty status {segment.status!r}")
        if segment.end <= segment.start:
            raise ValueError(f"segment at {segment.start} has no length")
    for before, after in zip(segments, segments[1:]):
        if after.start != before.end:
            raise ValueError(f"log is not contiguous at {before.end}")


def _driving_since_breaks(
    segments: list[DutySegment],
) -> tuple[list[tuple[DutySegment, timedelta]], timedelta]:
    """Each driving segment with the driving done since the last break before it,
    and the driving since the last break at the end of the log.

    A break is a non-driving segment of 30 minutes or more, in any status.
    """
    driving = timedelta(0)
    driven = []
    for segment in segments:
        if segment.status != DRIVING:
            if segment.length >= BREAK:
                driving = timedelta(0)
            continue
        driven.append((segment, driving))
        driving += segment.length
    return driven, driving


def break_violations(segments: list[DutySegment]) -> list[datetime]:
    """The moments the driver passed 8 hours of driving without a break.

    One violation per stretch: after a violation, the next is only reported once
    the driver has taken a break and driven 8 more hours.
    """
    _validate(segments)
    violations = []
    flagged = False
    driven, _ = _driving_since_breaks(segments)
    for segment, before in driven:
        if before == timedelta(0):
            flagged = False
        if not flagged and before + segment.length > MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK:
            violations.append(segment.start + (MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK - before))
            flagged = True
    return violations


def driving_left_before_break(segments: list[DutySegment]) -> timedelta:
    """How much more the driver may drive, at the end of the log, before a break."""
    _validate(segments)
    _, driving = _driving_since_breaks(segments)
    return max(MAX_DRIVING_WITHOUT_BREAK - driving, timedelta(0))

invoice_lines.py:
"""Customer invoice lines and totals for settled loads.

Each charge on a load becomes one invoice line: quantity times unit rate (miles x
rate per mile, hours x detention rate, pallets x handling rate). Rates in the rate
engine carry up to four decimal places, so line amounts are rounded to the cent,
half up, before they are printed.

Customers on quick-pay terms get a 2% discount for paying within 10 days; it is
printed as its own negative line under the subtotal.

Customer AP systems (Hartline's included) reconcile every invoice by adding up the
printed lines, so the subtotal must equal the sum of the line amounts as printed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
QUICK_PAY_RATE = Decimal("0.02")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Charge:
    description: str
    quantity: Decimal
    unit_rate: Decimal


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InvoiceLine:
    description: str
    amount: Decimal


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Invoice:
    lines: list[InvoiceLine]
    subtotal: Decimal
    quick_pay_discount: Decimal
    total: Decimal


def _to_cents(amount: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    # ROUND_HALF_UP rounds away from zero, so credits round the same way as charges.
    return amount.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def _extended(charge: Charge) -> Decimal:
    """Quantity times rate, unrounded."""
    return Decimal(charge.quantity) * Decimal(charge.unit_rate)


def _printed_lines(charges: list[Charge]) -> list[InvoiceLine]:
    return [InvoiceLine(charge.description, _to_cents(_extended(charge))) for charge in charges]


def _quick_pay_discount(subtotal: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return _to_cents(subtotal * QUICK_PAY_RATE)


def build_invoice(charges: list[Charge], quick_pay: bool = False) -> Invoice:
    """Build the printed invoice for one load's charges.

    Credits (negative unit rates) are allowed. With ``quick_pay``, a 2% discount
    of the subtotal is taken off the total.
    """
    if not charges:
        raise ValueError("an invoice needs at least one charge")
    lines = _printed_lines(charges)
    # Round once, at the end, so per-line rounding error doesn't pile up.
    subtotal = _to_cents(sum((_extended(charge) for charge in charges), Decimal("0")))
    discount = _quick_pay_discount(subtotal) if quick_pay else Decimal("0.00")
    return Invoice(
        lines=lines,
        subtotal=subtotal,
        quick_pay_discount=discount,
        total=subtotal - discount,
    )

detention.py:
"""Detention charges for drivers held at shipper and receiver facilities.

Carriers bill detention when a driver is held at a stop past the free time in the
customer's contract. Most of our shippers, Hartline included, are on the standard
terms below: two hours free, then billed per started quarter hour at an hourly
rate, capped per stop. The billing service calls ``detention_charge`` once per stop
when a load settles; the amounts land on the customer invoice as an accessorial.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

FREE_TIME = timedelta(hours=2)
INCREMENT_MINUTES = 15
DEFAULT_HOURLY_RATE = Decimal("75.00")
DEFAULT_STOP_CAP = Decimal("600.00")
CENT = Decimal("0.01")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StopTimes:
    """Facility timestamps for one stop, all in the same time zone.

    ``appointment`` is None at first-come-first-served (FCFS) facilities.
    """

    arrived: datetime
    departed: datetime
    appointment: datetime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DetentionTerms:
    free_time: timedelta = FREE_TIME
    hourly_rate: Decimal = DEFAULT_HOURLY_RATE
    # None means the contract has no per-stop cap.
    stop_cap: Decimal | None = DEFAULT_STOP_CAP


def _validate(stop: StopTimes) -> None:
    if stop.departed < stop.arrived:
        raise ValueError(f"departed {stop.departed} is before arrived {stop.arrived}")


def _clock_start(stop: StopTimes) -> datetime:
    """When free time starts counting for a stop: the gate check-in time.

    Check-in comes from the facility's gate log, which both sides can audit, so it
    is the one timestamp we bill from.
    """
    return stop.arrived


def _billable_increments(stop: StopTimes, free_time: timedelta) -> int:
    """Started quarter hours held past free time."""
    held = stop.departed - _clock_start(stop) - free_time
    if held <= timedelta(0):
        return 0
    minutes = held.total_seconds() / 60
    # A started increment is billed in full.
    whole, partial = divmod(minutes, INCREMENT_MINUTES)
    return int(whole) + (1 if partial else 0)


def _apply_cap(amount: Decimal, cap: Decimal | None) -> Decimal:
    if cap is not None and amount > cap:
        return cap
    return amount


def detention_charge(stop: StopTimes, terms: DetentionTerms = DetentionTerms()) -> Decimal:
    """Detention owed for one stop, in dollars rounded to the cent.

    Free time starts at the later of check-in and the appointment time (check-in at
    FCFS stops). Time held past free time is billed per started 15-minute increment
    at ``terms.hourly_rate``, then capped at ``terms.stop_cap``.

    >>> stop = StopTimes(arrived=datetime(2026, 3, 2, 8, 0), departed=datetime(2026, 3, 2, 11, 0))
    >>> detention_charge(stop)
    Decimal('75.00')
    """
    _validate(stop)
    increments = _billable_increments(stop, terms.free_time)
    if increments == 0:
        return Decimal("0.00")
    per_increment = terms.hourly_rate * INCREMENT_MINUTES / 60
    amount = (per_increment * increments).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return _apply_cap(amount, terms.stop_cap)

rate_confirmation.py:
"""Parse plain-text rate confirmations from brokered loads.

When we broker a load out, the carrier gets a rate confirmation ("rate con") and
signs it back; settlement later pays the carrier from what we parse here. Rate cons
come from our own TMS template and from a few partner TMSes, but all of them are
"Label: value" lines. Typical lines:

    Load #: TW-88412
    Carrier: Blue Ridge Haulers
    Linehaul: $2,150.00
    Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs
    Lumper: $185.00 (reimbursable w/ receipt)
    Total Carrier Pay: $2,822.50

Flat charges must add up to the stated total, or the rate con is rejected and goes
to the carrier-settlement queue for a person to look at. Hourly rates (detention,
layover per day) are not part of the total; they are kept for settlement to apply.
"""

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import Decimal

_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*([^:]+?)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*$")
_MONEY = re.compile(r"\$\s*(\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?)")
_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?")
_RATE_MARKERS = ("/hr", "per hour", "/day", "per day")
HEADER_FIELDS = {"load #": "load_number", "load number": "load_number", "carrier": "carrier"}
TOTAL_LABELS = {"total", "total carrier pay", "total rate"}


class RateConError(ValueError):
    """The rate con can't be used for settlement as is."""


@dataclass
class RateCon:
    load_number: str = ""
    carrier: str = ""
    charges: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)
    rates: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)
    total: Decimal | None = None


def _parse_money(value: str) -> Decimal:
    """The dollar amount on a line."""
    amounts = _NUMBER.findall(value)
    if not amounts:
        raise RateConError(f"no amount in {value!r}")
    # Amounts are written last on the line ("Linehaul: $2,150.00").
    return Decimal(amounts[-1].replace(",", ""))


def _is_rate(value: str) -> bool:
    lowered = value.lower()
    return any(marker in lowered for marker in _RATE_MARKERS)


def _read_line(con: RateCon, label: str, value: str) -> None:
    key = label.lower()
    if key in HEADER_FIELDS:
        setattr(con, HEADER_FIELDS[key], value)
    elif key in TOTAL_LABELS:
        con.total = _parse_money(value)
    elif _is_rate(value):
        con.rates[key] = _parse_money(value)
    elif _MONEY.search(value) or _NUMBER.fullmatch(value.split(" ")[0]):
        con.charges[key] = _parse_money(value)
    # Anything else (addresses, pickup times, notes) is not ours to parse.


def _check_total(con: RateCon) -> None:
    if con.total is None:
        raise RateConError("rate con has no total")
    flat = sum(con.charges.values(), Decimal("0"))
    if flat != con.total:
        raise RateConError(f"charges add up to {flat}, rate con total is {con.total}")


def parse_rate_confirmation(text: str) -> RateCon:
    """Parse a rate con's text and check that flat charges tie out to the total.

    Charge and rate labels are lowercased ("Fuel Surcharge" -> "fuel surcharge").
    Raises RateConError when the total is missing or doesn't match.
    """
    con = RateCon()
    for line in text.splitlines():
        match = _LINE.match(line)
        if match and match.group(2):
            _read_line(con, match.group(1), match.group(2))
    _check_total(con)
    return con

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from rate_confirmation import RateConError, parse_rate_confirmation

SIMPLE = """RATE CONFIRMATION
Load #: TW-90117
Carrier: Cascade Line Transport
Pickup: 2026-09-14 08:00 Tacoma, WA
Linehaul: $1,800.00
Fuel Surcharge: $310.25
Total Carrier Pay: $2,110.25
"""

HARTLINE_LOAD = """RATE CONFIRMATION
Load #: TW-88412
Carrier: Blue Ridge Haulers
Pickup: 2026-09-14 08:00 Tacoma, WA
Delivery: 2026-09-15 14:00 Boise, ID
Linehaul: $2,150.00
Fuel Surcharge: $412.50
Stop Off: $100.00 (1 extra stop)
Lumper: $185.00 (reimbursable w/ receipt)
Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs free
Total Carrier Pay: $2,847.50
"""


def test_header_fields():
    con = parse_rate_confirmation(SIMPLE)
    assert con.load_number == "TW-90117"
    assert con.carrier == "Cascade Line Transport"


def test_flat_charges_and_total():
    con = parse_rate_confirmation(SIMPLE)
    assert con.charges == {"linehaul": Decimal("1800.00"), "fuel surcharge": Decimal("310.25")}
    assert con.total == Decimal("2110.25")


def test_hourly_rates_are_kept_out_of_the_total():
    text = SIMPLE.replace("Total Carrier Pay", "Detention: $60.00/hr\nTotal Carrier Pay")
    con = parse_rate_confirmation(text)
    assert con.rates == {"detention": Decimal("60.00")}
    assert "detention" not in con.charges


def test_amount_without_dollar_sign():
    text = SIMPLE.replace("$1,800.00", "1800.00 USD")
    assert parse_rate_confirmation(text).charges["linehaul"] == Decimal("1800.00")


def test_mismatched_total_is_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(RateConError):
        parse_rate_confirmation(SIMPLE.replace("$2,110.25", "$2,200.00"))
    with pytest.raises(RateConError):
        parse_rate_confirmation(SIMPLE.replace("Total Carrier Pay: $2,110.25\n", ""))


def test_notes_after_the_amount_are_ignored():
    con = parse_rate_confirmation(HARTLINE_LOAD)
    assert con.charges["stop off"] == Decimal("100.00")
    assert con.charges["lumper"] == Decimal("185.00")


def test_detention_rate_with_free_time_note():
    con = parse_rate_confirmation(HARTLINE_LOAD)
    assert con.rates == {"detention": Decimal("75.00")}
    assert con.total == Decimal("2847.50")

axle_weights.py:
"""Federal axle weight checks for a loaded tractor-trailer (23 CFR 658.17).

Load planning runs ``check_axle_weights`` on the scale ticket or the planned axle
loads before a truck is dispatched onto the Interstate. The federal limits:

- 20,000 lbs on any single axle.
- 34,000 lbs on a tandem (two axles more than 40" and at most 96" apart).
- 80,000 lbs gross.
- The bridge formula, W = 500 * (L*N/(N-1) + 12*N + 36), on every group of two or
  more consecutive axles: N is the number of axles in the group, L the distance
  in feet between its outer axles, W the most the group may carry. Like the
  published bridge table, W is rounded to the nearest 500 lbs. A group that is
  just one tandem is covered by the tandem limit instead.
- Exception: two consecutive tandems may carry 34,000 lbs each (68,000 together)
  if their outer axles are 36 feet or more apart, even when the formula gives
  less.

Axles are given front to back, with positions in feet from the steer axle.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

SINGLE_LIMIT = 20_000
TANDEM_LIMIT = 34_000
GROSS_LIMIT = 80_000
TANDEM_MAX_SPACING_FT = 8.0
DOUBLE_TANDEM_MIN_SPAN_FT = 36.0
DOUBLE_TANDEM_LIMIT = 68_000


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Violation:
    rule: str  # "single", "tandem", "gross" or "bridge"
    first_axle: int
    last_axle: int
    weight: int
    limit: int


def bridge_limit(span_ft: float, axles: int) -> int:
    """The bridge formula for ``axles`` axles spread over ``span_ft`` feet."""
    if axles < 2:
        raise ValueError("the bridge formula needs at least two axles")
    raw = 500 * (Decimal(str(span_ft)) * axles / (axles - 1) + 12 * axles + 36)
    return int((raw / 500).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP) * 500)


def _tandem_starts(positions: list[float]) -> set[int]:
    """Indexes of axles that are the front axle of a tandem."""
    return {
        i for i in range(len(positions) - 1)
        if positions[i + 1] - positions[i] <= TANDEM_MAX_SPACING_FT
    }


def _bridge_spans(axle_count: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """The groups the bridge formula is checked on: the outer bridge, steer to last axle.

    Interior groups are already held down by the single and tandem limits.
    """
    return [(0, axle_count - 1)]


def _span_limit(first: int, last: int, positions: list[float], tandems: set[int]) -> int:
    span = positions[last] - positions[first]
    limit = bridge_limit(span, last - first + 1)
    double_tandem = last - first == 3 and first in tandems and first + 2 in tandems
    if double_tandem and span >= DOUBLE_TANDEM_MIN_SPAN_FT:
        limit = max(limit, DOUBLE_TANDEM_LIMIT)
    return limit


def check_axle_weights(weights: list[int], positions: list[float]) -> list[Violation]:
    """Every federal limit the axle loads break; an empty list means legal."""
    if len(weights) != len(positions) or len(weights) < 2:
        raise ValueError("need a weight and a position for each of at least two axles")
    if any(b <= a for a, b in zip(positions, positions[1:])):
        raise ValueError("axle positions must increase front to back")
    tandems = _tandem_starts(positions)
    in_tandem = tandems | {i + 1 for i in tandems}
    violations = []
    for i, weight in enumerate(weights):
        if i not in in_tandem and weight > SINGLE_LIMIT:
            violations.append(Violation("single", i, i, weight, SINGLE_LIMIT))
    for i in sorted(tandems):
        weight = weights[i] + weights[i + 1]
        if weight > TANDEM_LIMIT:
            violations.append(Violation("tandem", i, i + 1, weight, TANDEM_LIMIT))
    gross = sum(weights)
    if gross > GROSS_LIMIT:
        violations.append(Violation("gross", 0, len(weights) - 1, gross, GROSS_LIMIT))
    for first, last in _bridge_spans(len(weights)):
        weight = sum(weights[first:last + 1])
        limit = _span_limit(first, last, positions, tandems)
        if weight > limit:
            violations.append(Violation("bridge", first, last, weight, limit))
    return violations

scorecard.py:
"""On-time delivery percentage for the monthly carrier scorecard.

Carrier management sends every contracted carrier a scorecard at month end, and
the on-time number drives tender priority on the Hartline lanes. A delivery is on
time if it lands before the end of the appointment window plus a 15-minute grace
period. Early is on time.

Late deliveries with an excused delay code are not the carrier's fault (the
shipper loaded late, the consignee refused the appointment, or a weather closure)
and are left out of the measurement entirely. Cancelled loads and loads still in
transit are not measured either.
"""

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

GRACE = timedelta(minutes=15)
# Delay codes from the EDI 214 feed that excuse a late delivery.
EXCUSED_CODES = frozenset({"CUST", "CONS", "WX"})
DELIVERED = "delivered"
CANCELLED = "cancelled"
IN_TRANSIT = "in_transit"

ON_TIME = "on_time"
LATE = "late"
EXCUSED = "excused"
SKIPPED = "skipped"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Delivery:
    load_id: str
    window_end: datetime
    status: str = DELIVERED
    delivered_at: datetime | None = None
    delay_code: str | None = None


def _is_late(delivery: Delivery) -> bool:
    return delivery.delivered_at > delivery.window_end + GRACE


def _classify(delivery: Delivery) -> str:
    if delivery.status != DELIVERED or delivery.delivered_at is None:
        return SKIPPED
    if not _is_late(delivery):
        return ON_TIME
    if delivery.delay_code in EXCUSED_CODES:
        return EXCUSED
    return LATE


def scorecard_counts(deliveries: list[Delivery]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """How many deliveries fall in each scorecard bucket."""
    counts = Counter(_classify(delivery) for delivery in deliveries)
    return {bucket: counts.get(bucket, 0) for bucket in (ON_TIME, LATE, EXCUSED, SKIPPED)}


def on_time_percentage(deliveries: list[Delivery]) -> float | None:
    """The carrier's on-time percentage, rounded to one decimal place.

    Only on-time and unexcused late deliveries are measured. Returns None when
    nothing in the period is measured, so the scorecard can show "n/a" instead of
    a misleading 0%.
    """

eta_planner.py:
"""Delivery ETA for a solo driver, with the hours-of-service stops the trip needs.

Dispatch shows customers an ETA for every load in transit, recomputed from each
ELD ping. The plan drives at the lane's average speed and stops when an HOS limit
binds (property-carrying rules, 49 CFR 395.3):

- 11-hour limit: at most 11 hours of driving between 10-hour resets.
- 14-hour window: no driving after the 14th hour since coming on duty. The window
  is wall-clock time, so breaks and other stops use it up too.
- 30-minute break: due after 8 hours of driving without one.

When a break comes due with 30 minutes or less left in the window, the driver
takes the 10-hour reset instead, since a break would leave no time to drive.
Everything is planned in whole minutes.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DRIVE_LIMIT = 11 * 60
WINDOW = 14 * 60
BREAK_DUE = 8 * 60
BREAK = 30
RESET = 10 * 60


@dataclass
class DriverClocks:
    """Minutes left on each HOS clock when the trip starts."""

    drive_left: int = DRIVE_LIMIT
    window_left: int = WINDOW
    since_break: int = 0


@dataclass
class Plan:
    arrival: datetime
    stops: list[tuple[str, datetime]] = field(default_factory=list)


def _drive_minutes(miles: float, mph: float) -> int:
    if mph <= 0:
        raise ValueError("average speed must be positive")
    if miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("miles must be non-negative")
    return round(miles / mph * 60)


def estimate_arrival(
    depart: datetime, miles: float, mph: float, clocks: DriverClocks | None = None
) -> Plan:
    """Plan the trip from ``depart``; returns the arrival and each stop taken.

    Stops are ("break", start) or ("reset", start). ``clocks`` is not modified.
    """
    clocks = clocks or DriverClocks()
    remaining = _drive_minutes(miles, mph)
    drive_left, since_break = clocks.drive_left, clocks.since_break
    window_left = clocks.window_left
    now = depart
    stops: list[tuple[str, datetime]] = []
    while remaining > 0:
        leg = max(0, min(remaining, drive_left, window_left, BREAK_DUE - since_break))
        now += timedelta(minutes=leg)
        remaining -= leg
        drive_left -= leg
        window_left -= leg
        since_break += leg
        if remaining == 0:
            break
        break_due = since_break >= BREAK_DUE
        if drive_left <= 0 or window_left <= 0 or (break_due and window_left <= BREAK):
            stops.append(("reset", now))
            now += timedelta(minutes=RESET)
            drive_left, since_break, window_left = DRIVE_LIMIT, 0, WINDOW
        elif break_due:
            stops.append(("break", now))
            now += timedelta(minutes=BREAK)
            since_break = 0
    return Plan(arrival=now, stops=stops)

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import pytest

from eta_planner import DriverClocks, estimate_arrival

DEPART = datetime(2026, 10, 12, 6, 0)


def after(hours=0, minutes=0):
    return DEPART + timedelta(hours=hours, minutes=minutes)


def test_short_trip_needs_no_stops():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 200, 50)
    assert plan.arrival == after(4)
    assert plan.stops == []


def test_break_after_eight_hours_of_driving():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 500, 50)
    assert plan.stops == [("break", after(8))]
    assert plan.arrival == after(10, 30)


def test_eleven_hour_limit_forces_a_reset():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 700, 50)
    assert plan.stops == [("break", after(8)), ("reset", after(11, 30))]
    assert plan.arrival == after(24, 30)


def test_partly_used_clocks_carry_into_the_plan():
    clocks = DriverClocks(drive_left=300, window_left=540, since_break=360)
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 150, 50, clocks)
    assert plan.stops == [("break", after(2))]
    assert plan.arrival == after(3, 30)
    assert clocks.since_break == 360


def test_break_due_at_the_end_of_the_window_becomes_a_reset():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 450, 50, DriverClocks(window_left=495))
    assert plan.stops == [("reset", after(8))]
    assert plan.arrival == after(19)


def test_bad_inputs_are_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        estimate_arrival(DEPART, 100, 0)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        estimate_arrival(DEPART, -5, 50)


def test_break_uses_up_the_fourteen_hour_window():
    # On duty for 3h of loading before departure: 11h of window left.
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 535, 50, DriverClocks(window_left=660))
    assert plan.stops == [("break", after(8)), ("reset", after(11))]
    assert plan.arrival == after(21, 12)


def test_window_runs_out_just_after_a_break():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 450, 50, DriverClocks(window_left=540))
    assert plan.stops == [("break", after(8)), ("reset", after(9))]
    assert plan.arrival == after(19, 30)

rate_confirmation.py:
"""Parse plain-text rate confirmations from brokered loads.

When we broker a load out, the carrier gets a rate confirmation ("rate con") and
signs it back; settlement later pays the carrier from what we parse here. Rate cons
come from our own TMS template and from a few partner TMSes, but all of them are
"Label: value" lines. Typical lines:

    Load #: TW-88412
    Carrier: Blue Ridge Haulers
    Linehaul: $2,150.00
    Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs
    Lumper: $185.00 (reimbursable w/ receipt)
    Total Carrier Pay: $2,822.50

Flat charges must add up to the stated total, or the rate con is rejected and goes
to the carrier-settlement queue for a person to look at. Hourly rates (detention,
layover per day) are not part of the total; they are kept for settlement to apply.
"""

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import Decimal

_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*([^:]+?)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*$")
_MONEY = re.compile(r"\$\s*(\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?)")
_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d{1,2})?")
_RATE_MARKERS = ("/hr", "per hour", "/day", "per day")
HEADER_FIELDS = {"load #": "load_number", "load number": "load_number", "carrier": "carrier"}
TOTAL_LABELS = {"total", "total carrier pay", "total rate"}


class RateConError(ValueError):
    """The rate con can't be used for settlement as is."""


@dataclass
class RateCon:
    load_number: str = ""
    carrier: str = ""
    charges: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)
    rates: dict[str, Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)
    total: Decimal | None = None


def _parse_money(value: str) -> Decimal:
    """The dollar amount on a line."""
    amounts = _NUMBER.findall(value)
    if not amounts:
        raise RateConError(f"no amount in {value!r}")
    # Amounts are written last on the line ("Linehaul: $2,150.00").
    return Decimal(amounts[-1].replace(",", ""))


def _is_rate(value: str) -> bool:
    lowered = value.lower()
    return any(marker in lowered for marker in _RATE_MARKERS)


def _read_line(con: RateCon, label: str, value: str) -> None:
    key = label.lower()
    if key in HEADER_FIELDS:
        setattr(con, HEADER_FIELDS[key], value)
    elif key in TOTAL_LABELS:
        con.total = _parse_money(value)
    elif _is_rate(value):
        con.rates[key] = _parse_money(value)
    elif _MONEY.search(value) or _NUMBER.fullmatch(value.split(" ")[0]):
        con.charges[key] = _parse_money(value)
    # Anything else (addresses, pickup times, notes) is not ours to parse.


def _check_total(con: RateCon) -> None:
    if con.total is None:
        raise RateConError("rate con has no total")
    flat = sum(con.charges.values(), Decimal("0"))
    if flat != con.total:
        raise RateConError(f"charges add up to {flat}, rate con total is {con.total}")


def parse_rate_confirmation(text: str) -> RateCon:
    """Parse a rate con's text and check that flat charges tie out to the total.

    Charge and rate labels are lowercased ("Fuel Surcharge" -> "fuel surcharge").
    Raises RateConError when the total is missing or doesn't match.
    """
    con = RateCon()
    for line in text.splitlines():
        match = _LINE.match(line)
        if match and match.group(2):
            _read_line(con, match.group(1), match.group(2))
    _check_total(con)
    return con

Fix: should prefer the money amount (dollar-prefixed) — the first `$` amount. Let's think: for flat charge "Linehaul: $2,150.00" works. For rates "Detention: $75.00/hr after 2 hrs free" find `$75.00` via _MONEY. For "Stop Off: $100.00 (1 extra stop)" → $100.00.

But what about lines without a dollar sign? `_NUMBER.fullmatch(value.split(" ")[0])` allows bare numbers. Perhaps use _MONEY first, fall back to _NUMBER.

axle_weights.py:
"""Federal axle weight checks for a loaded tractor-trailer (23 CFR 658.17).

Load planning runs ``check_axle_weights`` on the scale ticket or the planned axle
loads before a truck is dispatched onto the Interstate. The federal limits:

- 20,000 lbs on any single axle.
- 34,000 lbs on a tandem (two axles more than 40" and at most 96" apart).
- 80,000 lbs gross.
- The bridge formula, W = 500 * (L*N/(N-1) + 12*N + 36), on every group of two or
  more consecutive axles: N is the number of axles in the group, L the distance
  in feet between its outer axles, W the most the group may carry. Like the
  published bridge table, W is rounded to the nearest 500 lbs. A group that is
  just one tandem is covered by the tandem limit instead.
- Exception: two consecutive tandems may carry 34,000 lbs each (68,000 together)
  if their outer axles are 36 feet or more apart, even when the formula gives
  less.

Axles are given front to back, with positions in feet from the steer axle.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

SINGLE_LIMIT = 20_000
TANDEM_LIMIT = 34_000
GROSS_LIMIT = 80_000
TANDEM_MAX_SPACING_FT = 8.0
DOUBLE_TANDEM_MIN_SPAN_FT = 36.0
DOUBLE_TANDEM_LIMIT = 68_000


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Violation:
    rule: str  # "single", "tandem", "gross" or "bridge"
    first_axle: int
    last_axle: int
    weight: int
    limit: int


def bridge_limit(span_ft: float, axles: int) -> int:
    """The bridge formula for ``axles`` axles spread over ``span_ft`` feet."""
    if axles < 2:
        raise ValueError("the bridge formula needs at least two axles")
    raw = 500 * (Decimal(str(span_ft)) * axles / (axles - 1) + 12 * axles + 36)
    return int((raw / 500).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP) * 500)


def _tandem_starts(positions: list[float]) -> set[int]:
    """Indexes of axles that are the front axle of a tandem."""
    return {
        i for i in range(len(positions) - 1)
        if positions[i + 1] - positions[i] <= TANDEM_MAX_SPACING_FT
    }


def _bridge_spans(axle_count: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """The groups the bridge formula is checked on: the outer bridge, steer to last axle.

    Interior groups are already held down by the single and tandem limits.
    """
    return [(0, axle_count - 1)]


def _span_limit(first: int, last: int, positions: list[float], tandems: set[int]) -> int:
    span = positions[last] - positions[first]
    limit = bridge_limit(span, last - first + 1)
    double_tandem = last - first == 3 and first in tandems and first + 2 in tandems
    if double_tandem and span >= DOUBLE_TANDEM_MIN_SPAN_FT:
        limit = max(limit, DOUBLE_TANDEM_LIMIT)
    return limit


def check_axle_weights(weights: list[int], positions: list[float]) -> list[Violation]:
    """Every federal limit the axle loads break; an empty list means legal."""
    if len(weights) != len(positions) or len(weights) < 2:
        raise ValueError("need a weight and a position for each of at least two axles")
    if any(b <= a for a, b in zip(positions, positions[1:])):
        raise ValueError("axle positions must increase front to back")
    tandems = _tandem_starts(positions)
    in_tandem = tandems | {i + 1 for i in tandems}
    violations = []
    for i, weight in enumerate(weights):
        if i not in in_tandem and weight > SINGLE_LIMIT:
            violations.append(Violation("single", i, i, weight, SINGLE_LIMIT))
    for i in sorted(tandems):
        weight = weights[i] + weights[i + 1]
        if weight > TANDEM_LIMIT:
            violations.append(Violation("tandem", i, i + 1, weight, TANDEM_LIMIT))
    gross = sum(weights)
    if gross > GROSS_LIMIT:
        violations.append(Violation("gross", 0, len(weights) - 1, gross, GROSS_LIMIT))
    for first, last in _bridge_spans(len(weights)):
        weight = sum(weights[first:last + 1])
        limit = _span_limit(first, last, positions, tandems)
        if weight > limit:
            violations.append(Violation("bridge", first, last, weight, limit))
    return violations

"""Delivery ETA for a solo driver, with the hours-of-service stops the trip needs.

Dispatch shows customers an ETA for every load in transit, recomputed from each
ELD ping. The plan drives at the lane's average speed and stops when an HOS limit
binds (property-carrying rules, 49 CFR 395.3):

- 11-hour limit: at most 11 hours of driving between 10-hour resets.
- 14-hour window: no driving after the 14th hour since coming on duty. The window
  is wall-clock time, so breaks and other stops use it up too.
- 30-minute break: due after 8 hours of driving without one.

When a break comes due with 30 minutes or less left in the window, the driver
takes the 10-hour reset instead, since a break would leave no time to drive.
Everything is planned in whole minutes.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DRIVE_LIMIT = 11 * 60
WINDOW = 14 * 60
BREAK_DUE = 8 * 60
BREAK = 30
RESET = 10 * 60


@dataclass
class DriverClocks:
    """Minutes left on each HOS clock when the trip starts."""

    drive_left: int = DRIVE_LIMIT
    window_left: int = WINDOW
    since_break: int = 0


@dataclass
class Plan:
    arrival: datetime
    stops: list[tuple[str, datetime]] = field(default_factory=list)


def _drive_minutes(miles: float, mph: float) -> int:
    if mph <= 0:
        raise ValueError("average speed must be positive")
    if miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("miles must be non-negative")
    return round(miles / mph * 60)


def estimate_arrival(
    depart: datetime, miles: float, mph: float, clocks: DriverClocks | None = None
) -> Plan:
    """Plan the trip from ``depart``; returns the arrival and each stop taken.

    Stops are ("break", start) or ("reset", start). ``clocks`` is not modified.
    """
    clocks = clocks or DriverClocks()
    remaining = _drive_minutes(miles, mph)
    drive_left, since_break = clocks.drive_left, clocks.since_break
    window_left = clocks.window_left
    now = depart
    stops: list[tuple[str, datetime]] = []
    while remaining > 0:
        leg = max(0, min(remaining, drive_left, window_left, BREAK_DUE - since_break))
        now += timedelta(minutes=leg)
        remaining -= leg
        drive_left -= leg
        window_left -= leg
        since_break += leg
        if remaining == 0:
            break
        break_due = since_break >= BREAK_DUE
        if drive_left <= 0 or window_left <= 0 or (break_due and window_left <= BREAK):
            stops.append(("reset", now))
            now += timedelta(minutes=RESET)
            drive_left, since_break, window_left = DRIVE_LIMIT, 0, WINDOW
        elif break_due:
            stops.append(("break", now))
            now += timedelta(minutes=BREAK)
            since_break = 0
    return Plan(arrival=now, stops=stops)

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import pytest

from eta_planner import DriverClocks, estimate_arrival

DEPART = datetime(2026, 10, 12, 6, 0)


def after(hours=0, minutes=0):
    return DEPART + timedelta(hours=hours, minutes=minutes)


def test_short_trip_needs_no_stops():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 200, 50)
    assert plan.arrival == after(4)
    assert plan.stops == []


def test_break_after_eight_hours_of_driving():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 500, 50)
    assert plan.stops == [("break", after(8))]
    assert plan.arrival == after(10, 30)


def test_eleven_hour_limit_forces_a_reset():
    plan = estimate_arrival(DEPART, 700, 50)

linear_feet.py:
"""Linear feet of trailer floor a palletized LTL shipment takes up.

LTL and volume quotes price by linear feet: how much of a 53' trailer's length the
freight occupies. Pallets load in rows across the trailer. A row holds two pallets
side by side when two fit inside the 100" usable width (a standard 48x40 does,
loaded with the 48" side along the trailer), otherwise one. A row is as deep as the
pallet's length.

Stackable pallets double-stack when two of them fit under the 102" usable height,
so two stacked pallets take one floor position. A stacked pair and a floor-only
pallet of the same footprint can share a row. Pallets with different footprints
don't share rows, since mixed rows don't load square.

Quoting calls ``linear_feet_for_shipment`` with the shipment's pallet lines.
"""

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass

TRAILER_WIDTH_IN = 100
TRAILER_HEIGHT_IN = 102
TRAILER_LENGTH_FT = 53


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PalletLine:
    """One line of the bill of lading: ``count`` pallets of the same build."""

    count: int
    length_in: int = 48
    width_in: int = 40
    height_in: int = 48
    stackable: bool = False

    @property
    def footprint(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        return (self.length_in, self.width_in)


def _per_row(width_in: int) -> int:
    return 2 if 2 * width_in <= TRAILER_WIDTH_IN else 1


def _floor_positions(line: PalletLine) -> int:
    """Floor positions one line needs, after double-stacking."""
    if line.stackable and 2 * line.height_in <= TRAILER_HEIGHT_IN:
        return math.ceil(line.count / 2)
    return line.count


def _validate(lines: list[PalletLine]) -> None:
    for line in lines:
        if line.count <= 0:
            raise ValueError("pallet count must be positive")
        if line.width_in > TRAILER_WIDTH_IN or line.height_in > TRAILER_HEIGHT_IN:
            raise ValueError(f"pallet {line.footprint} does not fit in a trailer")


def _row_inches(lines: list[PalletLine]) -> int:
    """Total trailer length in inches, line by line."""
    total = 0
    for line in lines:
        rows = math.ceil(_floor_positions(line) / _per_row(line.width_in))
        total += rows * line.length_in
    return total


def linear_feet_for_shipment(lines: list[PalletLine]) -> int:
    """Linear feet for the shipment, rounded up to the whole foot.

    Raises ValueError if the freight would not fit on one 53' trailer.
    """
    if not lines:
        raise ValueError("shipment has no pallets")
    _validate(lines)
    feet = math.ceil(_row_inches(lines) / 12)
    if feet > TRAILER_LENGTH_FT:
        raise ValueError(f"{feet} linear feet exceeds a {TRAILER_LENGTH_FT}' trailer")
    return feet

postal_codes.py:
"""Normalize US ZIP and Canadian postal codes from customer imports.

Customers send us stop lists as spreadsheets, and spreadsheets mangle postal codes:
a ZIP is stored as a number, so New England, New Jersey and Puerto Rico ZIPs lose
their leading zeros ("02134" becomes 2134, "00601" becomes 601), and sometimes come
back as floats ("2134.0"). Geocoding and lane rating both key on the normalized
form, so every address goes through ``normalize_postal_code`` on import.

Normalized forms:
    US:     "02134" or "02134-1234"
    Canada: "K1A 0B1"
"""

import re

_CANADIAN = re.compile(r"^([A-Z]\d[A-Z])\s?(\d[A-Z]\d)$")
_FLOAT_SUFFIX = re.compile(r"\.0+$")
# A 5-digit ZIP that lost leading zeros comes in as 3 or 4 digits.
_SHORT_ZIP5 = (3, 4)


def _clean_text(raw: str | int) -> str:
    text = str(raw).strip().upper()
    return _FLOAT_SUFFIX.sub("", text)


def _canadian(text: str) -> str | None:
    match = _CANADIAN.match(text)
    if not match:
        return None
    return f"{match.group(1)} {match.group(2)}"


def _us_parts(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Split a US ZIP into its 5-digit ZIP and optional +4, restoring lost zeros."""
    if "-" in text:
        zip5, _, plus4 = text.partition("-")
        if len(zip5) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
            zip5 = zip5.zfill(5)
        return zip5, plus4
    digits = text.replace(" ", "")
    if len(digits) in _SHORT_ZIP5:
        return digits.zfill(5), None
    if len(digits) <= 5:
        return digits, None
    # Without a hyphen, the first five digits are the ZIP and the rest is the +4.
    return digits[:5], digits[5:].zfill(4)


def _validate_us(zip5: str, plus4: str | None, raw: str | int) -> None:
    if len(zip5) != 5 or not zip5.isdigit():
        raise ValueError(f"not a US ZIP code: {raw!r}")
    if plus4 is not None and (len(plus4) != 4 or not plus4.isdigit()):
        raise ValueError(f"bad ZIP+4 extension: {raw!r}")


def normalize_postal_code(raw: str | int) -> str:
    """Return the normalized US ZIP or Canadian postal code, or raise ValueError.

    Accepts strings or ints. Leading zeros lost by a spreadsheet are restored, for
    both 5-digit ZIPs and ZIP+4.
    """
    text = _clean_text(raw)
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("empty postal code")
    canadian = _canadian(text)
    if canadian:
        return canadian
    zip5, plus4 = _us_parts(text)
    _validate_us(zip5, plus4, raw)
    return f"{zip5}-{plus4}" if plus4 else zip5

dock_schedule.py:
"""Dock door appointment conflicts at cross-dock facilities.

Appointment scheduling books inbound and outbound trucks onto dock doors. Each
appointment holds its door for a half-open window [start, end), and the yard crew
needs a turnaround buffer (15 minutes by default) after a truck pulls out before
the door can take the next one. Two appointments at the same door conflict if
their windows, each extended by the buffer at the end, overlap.

The scheduler runs ``find_conflicts`` before publishing the day's door plan, and
every pair it returns goes to the dock supervisor to resolve.
"""

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DEFAULT_BUFFER = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Appointment:
    appt_id: str
    door: str
    start: datetime
    end: datetime


def _validate(appointments: list[Appointment]) -> None:
    seen = set()
    for appt in appointments:
        if appt.end <= appt.start:
            raise ValueError(f"{appt.appt_id}: window ends before it starts")
        if appt.appt_id in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate appointment id {appt.appt_id}")
        seen.add(appt.appt_id)


def _by_door(appointments: list[Appointment]) -> dict[str, list[Appointment]]:
    doors: dict[str, list[Appointment]] = defaultdict(list)
    for appt in appointments:
        doors[appt.door].append(appt)
    return doors


def _door_conflicts(appointments: list[Appointment], buffer: timedelta) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Conflicting pairs at one door, earlier appointment first.

    Sweeps in start order, checking each appointment against the one before it:
    once sorted, only neighbors can overlap.
    """
    ordered = sorted(appointments, key=lambda appt: (appt.start, appt.appt_id))
    conflicts = []
    previous: Appointment | None = None
    for appt in ordered:
        if previous is not None and previous.end + buffer > appt.start:
            conflicts.append((previous.appt_id, appt.appt_id))
        previous = appt
    return conflicts


def appointments_at(appointments: list[Appointment], door: str) -> list[Appointment]:
    """One door's appointments in start order, for the door plan printout."""
    return sorted(_by_door(appointments).get(door, []), key=lambda appt: appt.start)


def find_conflicts(
    appointments: list[Appointment], buffer: timedelta = DEFAULT_BUFFER
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Every conflicting pair of appointments, as (earlier id, later id).

    Doors are reported in sorted order; within a door, pairs come in the order the
    later appointment starts.
    """
    _validate(appointments)
    conflicts = []
    for door, at_door in sorted(_by_door(appointments).items()):
        conflicts.extend(_door_conflicts(at_door, buffer))
    return conflicts

arguments.new_text:
"""Per-mile fuel surcharge (FSC) from the weekly DOE diesel average.

The DOE publishes the national on-highway diesel average every Monday, or on
Tuesday when Monday is a federal holiday. A published price applies to every
shipment picked up from its publication date until the next publication, so a
shipment uses the most recent price published on or before its pickup date.

Most contracts, Hartline's included, use the standard table: no surcharge at or
below a $1.20 peg, then one cent per mile for every full six cents above the peg.
Billing calls ``fuel_surcharge_for_shipment``; the price history comes from the
nightly DOE import as a {publication date: price} mapping.
"""

from bisect import bisect_right
from datetime import date
from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

PEG = Decimal("1.20")
STEP = Decimal("0.06")
CENTS_PER_STEP = Decimal("0.01")
CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def _as_decimal(value: Decimal | float | str) -> Decimal:
    # str() first, so a float price like 3.85 doesn't become 3.8499999...
    return value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))


def _publication_for(pickup: date, prices: dict[date, Decimal]) -> date:
    """The DOE publication in effect on ``pickup``: the latest one on or before it."""
    if not prices:
        raise ValueError("no DOE prices loaded")
    published = sorted(prices)
    index = bisect_right(published, pickup) - 1
    if index < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"no DOE price published on or before {pickup}")
    return published[index]


def _price_for(pickup: date, prices: dict[date, Decimal]) -> Decimal:
    return _as_decimal(prices[_publication_for(pickup, prices)])


def surcharge_per_mile(diesel_price: Decimal | float | str) -> Decimal:
    """Cents per mile from the standard table, as dollars (0.44 = 44 cents)."""
    price = _as_decimal(diesel_price)
    if price <= PEG:
        return Decimal("0.00")
    steps = ((price - PEG) / STEP).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR)
    return steps * CENTS_PER_STEP

    pickup: date, miles: Decimal | float | str, prices: dict[date, Decimal]

    loaded_miles = _as_decimal(miles)
    if loaded_miles < 0:
        raise ValueError("miles must be non-negative")
    per_mile = surcharge_per_mile(_price_for(pickup, prices))
    return (per_mile * loaded_miles).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

    """The invoice line text, e.g. "FSC $0.47/mi (DOE $4.03, week of 2026-09-14)"."""
    week_of = _publication_for(pickup, prices)
    price = _as_decimal(prices[week_of])

proration.py:
"""Split a load-level accessorial charge across the orders on a consolidated load.

Consolidated loads carry several customer orders on one trailer. Some accessorials
(tarping, a lumper at a shared dock, a stop-off charge) are billed once for the
whole load, and billing has to split them across the orders, in proportion to each
order's weight by default, or to pallet count for some customers.

The split is in whole cents and must add back up to the charge exactly, because
each order is invoiced separately and finance reconciles the carrier bill against
the sum. We use the largest-remainder method: every order gets the cents its exact
share rounds down to, and the cents left over go one each to the orders whose
exact share lost the most in rounding down. Ties go to the earlier order on the
load, so reruns give the same split.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Order:
    order_id: str
    weight_lbs: int
    pallets: int = 0


def _to_cents(amount: Decimal) -> int:
    cents = amount / CENT
    if cents != cents.to_integral_value():
        raise ValueError(f"charge {amount} is not a whole number of cents")
    return int(cents)


def _basis(orders: list[Order], by: str) -> list[int]:
    if by == "weight":
        return [order.weight_lbs for order in orders]
    if by == "pallets":
        return [order.pallets for order in orders]
    raise ValueError(f"unknown proration basis {by!r}")


def _largest_remainder(total_cents: int, weights: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Whole-cent shares of ``total_cents`` proportional to ``weights``.

    Integer arithmetic throughout, so nothing is lost to float rounding.
    """
    whole = sum(weights)
    if whole == 0:
        # Nothing to weigh by: split evenly.
        weights = [1] * len(weights)
        whole = len(weights)
    shares = [total_cents * weight // whole for weight in weights]
    leftover = total_cents - sum(shares)
    # Fewer leftover cents than orders; hand them out in load order so reruns match.
    for index in range(leftover):
        shares[index] += 1
    return shares


def prorate_charge(charge: Decimal, orders: list[Order], by: str = "weight") -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Split ``charge`` across ``orders``; returns {order_id: amount}.

    A credit (negative charge) is split the same way as the matching charge, with
    every share negative.
    """
    if not orders:
        raise ValueError("no orders to prorate across")
    weights = _basis(orders, by)
    if any(weight < 0 for weight in weights):
        raise ValueError("proration basis must be non-negative")
    sign = -1 if charge < 0 else 1
    cents = _largest_remainder(abs(_to_cents(charge)), weights)
    return {order.order_id: sign * share * CENT for order, share in zip(orders, cents)}

postal_codes.py:
"""Normalize US ZIP and Canadian postal codes from customer imports.

Customers send us stop lists as spreadsheets, and spreadsheets mangle postal codes:
a ZIP is stored as a number, so New England, New Jersey and Puerto Rico ZIPs lose
their leading zeros ("02134" becomes 2134, "00601" becomes 601), and sometimes come
back as floats ("2134.0"). Geocoding and lane rating both key on the normalized
form, so every address goes through ``normalize_postal_code`` on import.

Normalized forms:
    US:     "02134" or "02134-1234"
    Canada: "K1A 0B1"
"""

import re

dock_schedule.py:
"""Dock door appointment conflicts at cross-dock facilities.

Appointment scheduling books inbound and outbound trucks onto dock doors. Each
appointment holds its door for a half-open window [start, end), and the yard crew
needs a turnaround buffer (15 minutes by default) after a truck pulls out before
the door can take the next one. Two appointments at the same door conflict if
their windows, each extended by the buffer at the end, overlap.

The scheduler runs ``find_conflicts`` before publishing the day's door plan, and
every pair it returns goes to the dock supervisor to resolve.
"""

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DEFAULT_BUFFER = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Appointment:
    appt_id: str
    door: str
    start: datetime
    end: datetime


def _validate(appointments: list[Appointment]) -> None:
    seen = set()
    for appt in appointments:
        if appt.end <= appt.start:
            raise ValueError(f"{appt.appt_id}: window ends before it starts")
        if appt.appt_id in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate appointment id {appt.appt_id}")
        seen.add(appt.appt_id)


def _by_door(appointments: list[Appointment]) -> dict[str, list[Appointment]]:
    doors: dict[str, list[Appointment]] = defaultdict(list)
    for appt in appointments:
        doors[appt.door].append(appt)
    return doors


def _door_conflicts(appointments: list[Appointment], buffer: timedelta) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Conflicting pairs at one door, earlier appointment first.

    Sweeps in start order, checking each appointment against the one before it:
    once sorted, only neighbors can overlap.
    """
    ordered = sorted(appointments, key=lambda appt: (appt.start, appt.appt_id))
    conflicts = []
    previous: Appointment | None = None
    for appt in ordered:
        if previous is not None and previous.end + buffer > appt.start:
            conflicts.append((previous.appt_id, appt.appt_id))
        previous = appt
    return conflicts


def appointments_at(appointments: list[Appointment], door: str) -> list[Appointment]:
    """One door's appointments in start order, for the door plan printout."""
    return sorted(_by_door(appointments).get(door, []), key=lambda appt: appt.start)


def find_conflicts(
    appointments: list[Appointment], buffer: timedelta = DEFAULT_BUFFER
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Every conflicting pair of appointments, as (earlier id, later id).

    Doors are reported in sorted order; within a door, pairs come in the order the
    later appointment starts.
    """
    _validate(appointments)
    conflicts = []
    for door, at_door in sorted(_by_door(appointments).items()):
        conflicts.extend(_door_conflicts(at_door, buffer))
    return conflicts

The bug: `_zone_offsets` resolves each consignee zone's UTC offset using `run_at` (the batch run time), not the delivery time. If the delivery happens during EST but the batch runs during EDT (or vice versa), the offset is wrong. In this case: delivery 2026-11-01 00:30 EDT (04:30 UTC). DST ends 2026-11-01 at 2am local, so at 00:30 EDT, offset is -4. `run_at` is Monday's batch — after DST ended, so offset is -5 (EST). So `delivered_at + offset` = 04:30 UTC - 5h = 2026-10-31 23:30 → date 2026-10-31. Wrong. Correct is 2026-11-01.

Fix: resolve the offset at the delivery time, not at run_at. i.e., `delivered_at.astimezone(ZoneInfo(name)).utcoffset()` per delivery. The cache/perf optimization is the bug. But note the docstring says resolving per delivery showed up in batch profile. We can cache by (zone, date) or by (zone, is_dst)? Simpler: cache per (zone name, delivery date/day)? Actually the correct offset depends on the delivery instant. We could cache per (zone name, delivered_at date?) Still ambiguous around the transition, but per-instance lookup is fine. Simplest correct fix: convert each delivery to the zone at delivery time.

from datetime import date, datetime, timezone

import pytest

from invoice_dates import Delivery, InvoiceDates, invoice_dates_for_batch


def utc(*args):
    return datetime(*args, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def test_invoice_date_is_the_consignee_local_date():
    batch = [Delivery("TW-1", utc(2026, 7, 15, 3, 30), "America/Los_Angeles")]
    dates = invoice_dates_for_batch(batch, run_at=utc(2026, 7, 16, 9, 0))
    assert dates["TW-1"] == InvoiceDates(date(2026, 7, 14), date(2026, 8, 13))


def test_weekend_due_date_rolls_to_monday():
    batch = [Delivery("TW-2", utc(2026, 7, 10, 18, 0), "America/Chicago")]
    dates = invoice_dates_for_batch(batch, run_at=utc(2026, 7, 11, 9, 0))
    assert dates["TW-2"].due_date == date(2026, 8, 10)


def test_mixed_zones_in_one_batch():
    batch = [
        Delivery("TW-3", utc(2026, 8, 3, 4, 15), "America/Chicago"),
        Delivery("TW-4", utc(2026, 8, 3, 4, 15), "America/New_York", terms_days=15),
    ]
    dates = invoice_dates_for_batch(batch, run_at=utc(2026, 8, 4, 9, 0))
    assert dates["TW-3"].invoice_date == date(2026, 8, 2)
    assert dates["TW-4"] == InvoiceDates(date(2026, 8, 3), date(2026, 8, 18))


def test_loads_delivered_after_the_run_wait_for_the_next_run():
    batch = [Delivery("TW-5", utc(2026, 7, 16, 10, 0), "America/Denver")]
    assert invoice_dates_for_batch(batch, run_at=utc(2026, 7, 16, 9, 0)) == {}


def test_naive_timestamps_are_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        invoice_dates_for_batch([Delivery("TW-6", datetime(2026, 7, 1, 12, 0), "America/Denver")], utc(2026, 7, 2))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        invoice_dates_for_batch([], datetime(2026, 7, 2))


def test_delivery_just_before_fall_back_uses_daylight_time():
    # 00:30 EDT on Sun 2026-11-01; the batch runs Monday, after clocks went back.
    batch = [Delivery("TW-7", utc(2026, 11, 1, 4, 30), "America/New_York")]
    dates = invoice_dates_for_batch(batch, run_at=utc(2026, 11, 2, 8, 0))
    assert dates["TW-7"] == InvoiceDates(date(2026, 11, 1), date(2026, 12, 1))


def test_delivery_just_before_spring_forward_uses_standard_time():
    # 23:30 EST on Sat 2026-03-07; the batch runs Monday, after clocks went forward.
    batch = [Delivery("TW-8", utc(2026, 3, 8, 4, 30), "America/New_York")]
    dates = invoice_dates_for_batch(batch, run_at=utc(2026, 3, 9, 8, 0))

proration.py:
"""Split a load-level accessorial charge across the orders on a consolidated load.

Consolidated loads carry several customer orders on one trailer. Some accessorials
(tarping, a lumper at a shared dock, a stop-off charge) are billed once for the
whole load, and billing has to split them across the orders, in proportion to each
order's weight by default, or to pallet count for some customers.

The split is in whole cents and must add back up to the charge exactly, because
each order is invoiced separately and finance reconciles the carrier bill against
the sum. We use the largest-remainder method: every order gets the cents its exact
share rounds down to, and the cents left over go one each to the orders whose
exact share lost the most in rounding down. Ties go to the earlier order on the
load, so reruns give the same split.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Order:
    order_id: str
    weight_lbs: int
    pallets: int = 0


def _to_cents(amount: Decimal) -> int:
    cents = amount / CENT
    if cents != cents.to_integral_value():
        raise ValueError(f"charge {amount} is not a whole number of cents")
    return int(cents)


def _basis(orders: list[Order], by: str) -> list[int]:
    if by == "weight":
        return [order.weight_lbs for order in orders]
    if by == "pallets":
        return [order.pallets for order in orders]
    raise ValueError(f"unknown proration basis {by!r}")


def _largest_remainder(total_cents: int, weights: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Whole-cent shares of ``total_cents`` proportional to ``weights``.

    Integer arithmetic throughout, so nothing is lost to float rounding.
    """
    whole = sum(weights)
    if whole == 0:
        # Nothing to weigh by: split evenly.
        weights = [1] * len(weights)
        whole = len(weights)
    shares = [total_cents * weight // whole for weight in weights]
    leftover = total_cents - sum(shares)
    # Fewer leftover cents than orders; hand them out in load order so reruns match.
    for index in range(leftover):
        shares[index] += 1
    return shares


def prorate_charge(charge: Decimal, orders: list[Order], by: str = "weight") -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Split ``charge`` across ``orders``; returns {order_id: amount}.

    A credit (negative charge) is split the same way as the matching charge, with
    every share negative.
    """
    if not orders:
        raise ValueError("no orders to prorate across")
    weights = _basis(orders, by)
    if any(weight < 0 for weight in weights):
        raise ValueError("proration basis must be non-negative")
    sign = -1 if charge < 0 else 1
    cents = _largest_remainder(abs(_to_cents(charge)), weights)
    return {order.order_id: sign * share * CENT for order, share in zip(orders, cents)}
